Hi Alicia — thanks for the note.

Short answers up front:
- We can accept a master resale certificate only if it explicitly names the subsidiaries (or includes wording that the certificate covers all DBAs/affiliated entities) and the states where you claim exemption.
- For TX and WA (and any state with specific form requirements), we typically need either the state-specific exemption form (TX ST-1/ST-141) or a signed affidavit from your tax team that references the master certificate and the list of covered entities.

Would you be able to:
1) Share the master resale certificate PDF (preferably signed).
2) Provide a short mapping table (spreadsheet or even a bullet list) that lists the exact legal name and the DBA that should appear on our invoices for each subsidiary.
3) If you have state-specific forms for TX/WA, please include them as well.

Looping in Marissa (sales ops) to note invoice fields we can update, and Rishi (finance) to approve clearance once docs are validated.

If you can get the files over today or tomorrow we can target releasing the invoices from hold by end of week.

Hi Alicia — Marissa here from Sales Ops. Quick clarifications to speed validation: 

- Preferred file formats: PDF for certificates, XLSX or CSV for mapping.
- Required fields on the certificate we check: issuing state, buyer legal name, buyer address, effective date, signature (or electronic signature) and a statement of purpose indicating resale.
- For Texas: we need either the blanket resale wording or the specific ST-198 form; state-specific header + seller exemption number helps.
- If you provide a one-page signed affidavit referencing the master certificate and explicitly listing the subsidiaries (legal names and any DBAs), that will be sufficient for non-TX states and will speed clearing.
